newsitem.title: UK: U.S. said reassured on Turkey security zone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. said reassured on Turkey security zone.

text.p: Secretary of State Warren Christopher said Saturday the United States understands Turkey's reasons for establishing a security zone in Iraq and has been assured it will be temporary and involve no permanent troops.
"We understand their reasons for doing so and we've been reassured the situation will only be temporary and their forces will not be stationed there," he said in an interview with reporters.
Christopher returned to London on Saturday from Stuttgart as part of a five-day trip to Europe.

He said the Turks had "genuine reasons to be concerned about their border and (cross-border attacks by) the PKK", the Kurdistan Workers' Party that has fought for 12 years to carve an independent state out of southeastern Turkey.

He said Turkey has long taken the same position as the United States in support of Iraq's territorial integrity and stressed the "important role" Turkey had played in the region and in supporting and participating in the U.S.-led Gulf War coalition against Iraq.

Following U.S. air attacks last week in retaliation against Baghdad for sending troops into Kurdish-controlled areas of northern Iraq, Turkey said it planned to set up a buffer zone against attacks from the PKK guerrillas.
